note: The only differences from the declarations before the TypeScript moves that the public-surface check accepts, each as the one failed assertion of one subject with the old and new value the compiler reports. An entry absorbs nothing else on its subject, and an entry the check no longer needs fails it. These are pair-assertion differences, not the only observable changes: the new augmentation reach is asserted in catalog-examples-types.test.mjs, and new exports are listed in public-surface-inventory.json.

accepted.subject: .:type:DataDiffValues
accepted.reason: Readonly<Record<string, DataDiffValue>> became { readonly [columnId: string]: DataDiffValue }. keyof a string index signature is string | number where the Record alias gave string; mutual assignability and every other key set are unchanged.

accepted.subject: .:type:ResizableSizes
accepted.reason: Readonly<Record<string, number>> became { readonly [panelId: string]: number }, with the same keyof widening.

accepted.subject: .:type:MuxUIValidationErrors
accepted.reason: Readonly<Record<string, string | string[]>> became { readonly [key: string]: string | string[] }, with the same keyof widening.

accepted.subject: .:props:PromptComposer
accepted.reason: PromptComposerProps no longer intersects the form's own defaultValue (string | number | readonly string[]) with the composer's string: the old type was string | (string & readonly string[]), the new one is string. Both are assignable to each other and accept the same values; only the readonly keys of the property type's apparent members (a branded string's length and index) differ.
